observation.visible_scene: A static wide landscape shot: a long, rugged mountain ridge with tan-brown slopes, darker scrub patches and small snow remnants on the upper-left peaks, set under a flat overcast white sky. The mountains and sky are mirrored in a calm, dark green lake that fills the lower half of the frame. A thin dark shoreline band separates the real mountains from their reflection. In the foreground are dry golden grass tufts at the bottom edge and a cluster of dark evergreen trees at the lower left.
visible_changes: The mountains, shoreline, evergreen trees, foreground grass and the overall framing keep the same position and size from the first to the last frame, indicating no camera pan, tilt or zoom and no movement of the terrain or vegetation.

The only visible motion is in the water surface: the bright sky-reflection patch at the lower-right corner and the mottled texture of the mountain reflection shift and waver very slightly and slowly across the segment, consistent with small ripples distorting the reflected image rather than any object moving.
The reflection remains a reflection of the same mountains/sky throughout; it does not separate into or reveal any additional objects.
No onset, contact, landing or completion of an action is visible; the gentle water undulation appears already ongoing at the start and still ongoing at the end of the crop.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether the water motion is caused by wind or a current, and whether it intensifies, calms, or stops outside this segment.
Whether the camera is handheld with sub-pixel drift or on a fixed mount.
Any scene content before t=0 or after the last frame.
uncertain_details: The magnitude of the reflection/ripple change is very small; it is partly ambiguous whether the subtle differences in the bright lower-right patch and the reflection texture are genuine water motion or encoding/compression noise.
No clearly moving object (person, animal, vehicle, bird) is present, so the 'process' is limited to the near-static landscape with minor surface disturbance.
